claims.text: A tailored post-solidification heat treatment can refine and strengthen interlamellar interfaces in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Refining and strengthening interlamellar interfaces will simultaneously improve strength and room-temperature tensile ductility.
The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy contains dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Internal boundaries in the lamellar colonies act as microcrack-initiation sites during room-temperature tensile deformation.
Adjusting heat-treatment temperature and holding time can promote a thin, cohesive interfacial layer.
The proposed interfacial layer reduces defects and residual stresses.
Heat-treatment parameters must avoid phase coarsening and unwanted phase transformations.
The treatment produces interlamellar interfaces with reduced defect density and altered local composition or structure.
The modified interfaces better resist microcrack initiation and propagation.
The heat treatment relaxes internal stresses and modifies the chemistry or structure at colony boundaries.
Stress relaxation and boundary modification reduce stress concentrations and delay microcrack nucleation.
Delayed microcrack nucleation produces more uniform load distribution and improved plasticity without compromising strength.
Heat-treated specimens will have higher tensile strength than untreated specimens at room temperature.
Heat-treated specimens will have greater elongation to failure than untreated specimens at room temperature.
The improvements in tensile strength and elongation are expected to be approximately 10–20%.
Heat treatment will notably delay microcrack initiation during deformation.
Conventionally processed specimens with unmodified, defect-prone lamellar interfaces exhibit high strength, limited ductility, and early microcracking.
The treatment is beneficial only within a composition- and processing-specific window that avoids adverse transformations and coarsening.
The magnitude of the mechanical-property improvements depends on alloy composition and the heat-treatment schedule.
